newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit little moved as focus turns to baht.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit little moved as focus turns to baht.

text.p: The ringgit was little moved in Asia as market focus turned to Thailand's troubled finance sector, dealers said.
A pause in the rise of the ringgit against the Singapore dollars also halted dollar/ringgit movements, they said.
"Attention is on the Thai baht. But ringgit should gain on any turmoil of its neighbour," said a dealer at a local bank.
The Thai government, in a major shake up of the troubled finance sector, on Monday ordered 10 finance firms to boost their capital and told banks and finance firms to raise provisions for bad debts.
The ringgit, which jumped against the Singapore dollar on Tuesday on buying by U.S. funds, drifted quietly.
"Sing/ringgit can still come down," said another dealer. But it needed to consolidate between 1.7330/70, the dealer said.

Speculation about a hike in Malaysia's statutory reserve requirement -- funds which banks place interest free with the central bank -- was dismissed by some players. One banking source said such a move would only make sense it there was excessive fund liquidity in Malaysia.
At 0800 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4750/60 a dollar against 2.4786/91 at Kuala Lumpur close on Tuesday.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.7349/68 ringgit from 1.7369/85.
